explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/491: if f : ℕ → ℝ is additive and |f(n+1) − f(n)| < c for all n, must f(n) = c' log n + O(1)? Answered yes by Wirsing. The statement requires additivity on coprime positive a, b, a uniform bound on consecutive differences (the n = 0 instance only constrains the irrelevant value f(0) to be finite-distance from f(1)), and concludes f n − c log n = O(1) at atTop. Faithful.
